page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.8xlarge is a high-clock-speed instance configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides hyper-threading support alongside hardware-level instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES cryptography, and BMI2. The system carries 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, which places it squarely in memory-dense territory while retaining elevated per-core clock frequencies.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All persistent storage operations must traverse network-attached block volumes, supported by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Memory subsystem benchmarks record a large-block read throughput of 112.52 GB/sec and a write throughput of 49.63 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads achieve 1704.61 GB/sec. Across standard compute benchmarks, the instance yields a Geekbench multi-core score of 11147.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 29575.82, placing its processing capacity within expected median tiers for 32-vCPU x86 server classes.

The combination of a 3.1 GHz base processor frequency and high RAM capacity makes the instance viable for memory-intensive compute jobs. In benchmark testing, the configuration handled 28.86 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 22.36 GB/sec throughput in static web serving benchmarks. Software compilation on Clang registered a Geekbench subscore of 23685.0. Workload applicability centers on large in-memory databases, caching layers, analytics engines, and enterprise backend applications that require both low-latency instruction execution and substantial working memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.8xlarge is a high-clock-speed server instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system memory, based on an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. It incorporates hyper-threading across 16 physical cores, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive enterprise computing. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 10 Gbps baseline network interface for network-attached storage and node communication. Benchmark results demonstrate reliable throughput, reaching 28.86 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 112.52 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. Due to its combination of high CPU clock speeds and extensive memory capacity, this instance fits environments running large in-memory key-value databases, memory-resident data analytics, continuous integration compilation pipelines, and transactional database servers.
